newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS says May passenger volume up 4.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: SAS says May passenger volume up 4.8 pct.

text.p: Scandianvian airline SAS said on Monday passenger volumes rose 4.8 percent in May compared to May 1996 and the passenger load factor edged down to 65.2 percent from 65.5 percent.
The airline said in a statement it would begin publishing the data on the sixth business day after the end of each month.
These passenger traffic volumes were RPK, or revenue passenger kilometres, which is the number of revenue passengers multiplied by the kilometres they are flown, SAS said.
The ASK or available seat kilometres rose 5.2 percent in May to 2.64 million and four percent to 12.71 million in the 1997 January to May period compared to the same 1996 period.
ASK is the total number of seats available for the transportation of passengers multiplied by the number of kilometres which these are flown, the airline said.
The total number of passengers rose to 1.78 million, up 2.3 percent. For the 1997 January to May period, the total number of passengers rose 3.4 percent to 8.10 million.
SAS said the airline had noted strong growth on European, intra-Scandianavian and Norwegian domestic routes.

The Danish and Swedish domestic route areas were still developing quite weakly, it said. "Furthermore, SAS has extended the co-operation with regional partners in these route areas," the airline said.
